corrected_content.problem:
Evaluate the integral $$
\displaystyle \int_(C)(x^{2} + y^{2})ds,
$$ where $C$ is the curve parametrized by $\mathbf{r}(t)=3(\operatorname{cos}t+t\operatorname{sin}t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+3(\operatorname{sin}t-t\operatorname{cos}t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}\hspace{0.167em}$ for $0 \le t \le 2π$.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Differentiating gives $r'(t)=3t\langle\cos t,\sin t\rangle$, so the speed is $3t$ on $[0,2\pi]$. Also $x^2+y^2=9(1+t^2)$. Hence $$\int_C(x^2+y^2)\,ds=27\int_0^{2\pi}(t+t^3)\,dt=54\pi^2+108\pi^4=54\pi^2(1+2\pi^2).$$
